task: Add an optional nested camelCase `oauth` config object to the ManagedMcpServer catalog model so GET /v1/mcp/managed-servers exposes self-describing per-server OAuth client parameters, preserving loader skip-and-log resilience and backward compatibility.

key_reasoning.reason: camelCase wire aliasing is a novel convention for src/codemie/configs/ — no alias_generator, to_camel, serialization_alias or populate_by_name exists in managed_mcp_config.py, llm_config.py, budget_config.py, datasources_config.py or mcp_config.py. Compounding this, ManagedMcpServer is a dual-role model (YAML schema and FastAPI response_model), so one alias choice governs both parse and serialize sides, and it interacts with ConfigDict(extra="ignore") under which a near-miss key such as client_id is silently dropped instead of skipped-and-logged — directly at odds with the stated resilience contract. Bumped from M to L for security-adjacent payload (OAuth client id, scope, IdP authorize/token URLs surfaced over the endpoint and written to warning logs, where managed_mcp_config.py:91-92 carries an explicit "revisit if a credential-bearing field is added" caveat).

One meaningful component: the self-contained 99-line src/codemie/configs/managed_mcp_config.py holding both the Pydantic model and the loader. The router mcp_managed.py needs no edit — response_model=List[ManagedMcpServer] inherits the new field and FastAPI serializes by_alias by default. Additive nested model on an existing endpoint response, no service or repository layer involved.

4 files, no new files, ~40-70 net new lines: managed_mcp_config.py, config/customer/managed-mcp-servers.example.yaml (hard-bound to the model by test_example_file_is_valid), tests/codemie/configs/test_managed_mcp_config.py, and tests/codemie/rest_api/routers/test_mcp_managed.py — the latter unstated in the ticket but broken by its exact-dict assertion at lines 55-64 the moment an oauth key appears.

Field names, types, required/optional status, defaults, bounds, target JSON shape, backward-compat rule and out-of-scope items are all enumerated. Open items (alias only the nested OAuth model vs the whole ManagedMcpServer; whether snake_case keys stay loadable via populate_by_name) are implementation design decisions, not requirement gaps.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M (3) to L (4): security-adjacent change — the endpoint now publishes OAuth client parameters (client id, scope, loopback callback, IdP authorization and token URLs), and those values enter warning logs at a call site explicitly annotated "revisit if a credential-bearing field is ever added". No secret is stored and token exchange stays client-side, so no further bump applied.
